title: Commit Bridge: Tiered Reserve Trials & SLA-Uplift Offerings for Dedicated Capacity
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise prospects demand predictable throughput and an easy on-ramp from evaluation to committed capacity. Current reserved SKU packaging is binary (reserved vs on-demand) and makes it hard to convert trials or provide short-term elevated SLAs for proof-of-value.

Proposal: Build a Commit Bridge product experiment: a set of short-term, low-friction reserved bands (1-6 week micro-commitments) that customers can purchase as trial-reserves. Each band includes: a) guaranteed baseline capacity (vCPU/GPU-equivalent slots) b) optional SLA uplift add-on (p99 latency target bump and incident response SLO) c) burst credits that integrate with autoscaling policies. The offering is priced to be cheaper than on-demand for aggressive usage profiles while allowing easy conversion into standard reserved contracts.

Goals: 1) Increase trial->paid conversion rate for mid-market/enterprise by 25% for dedicated interest flows. 2) Surface demand signals for regions and GPU tiers. 3) Reduce sales friction for short pilots and speed legal/security questionnaire signoff by standardizing an "SLA-Uplift Rider" template.

Scope: - Product pricing grid for micro-commitments (1/2/4/6 weeks) per GPU family and region. - Billing and reserve accounting changes (credit-style accounting that rolls up into standard commit if customer upgrades). - Console UX for purchasing, showing projected costs, and conversion flow. - Legal playbook: SLA-Uplift Rider text, escalation matrix, and standard answers for common enterprise security questionnaire items regarding isolation, data geography, and KMS. - Pilot with 5 qualified accounts and sales-led onboarding flow.
acceptance_criteria: Pricing table published for 1/2/4/6 week micro-commit bundles across 3 GPU tiers (A100, H100, L4) and 3 regions
Console: purchase flow and conversion CTA implemented behind feature flag
Billing: micro-commit credits appear on invoices and convert to reserved commitment when customer upgrades; accounting reconciles in billing sandbox
Legal: SLA-Uplift Rider draft reviewed by legal and security with standard SQ answers drafted for common questions
Pilot: 3 live pilots with telemetry (conversion intent, overage frequency, p99 latency) instrumented
tasks: Finalize price multipliers for uplift (+10/20/35% tiers) and burst-credit burn rates
Define autoscale guardrails and max-burst caps per micro-commit band
Implement billing credit ledger and conversion API (engineering ticket dependency)
Design console purchase UX and conversion modal (link to DES ticket)
Draft SLA-Uplift Rider and run legal review
Prepare sales enablement pack and pilot onboarding checklist
decisions: Use credit-style accounting to minimize billing churn when customers convert
Offer three discrete SLA uplift tiers rather than continuous SLA negotiation to speed legal review
Cap burst at 2x baseline for micro-commit bands to protect oversubscription risk
risks: Potential revenue cannibalization vs full reserved SKU if pricing not sufficiently differentiated
Operational risk: short commitments increase churn and billing complexity
SLA uplift exposes support to higher obligation; need clear runbook or additional support SKU
Security questionnaire variations by region (data residency / on-prem routing) could delay pilot setup
customer_profiles: AI-native startup running inference-heavy features that need short pilot capacity
Mid-market SaaS company wanting predictable p99 SLAs for a quarter-long launch
Platform team evaluating Dedicated with expectation to convert after a 3-week pilot
pilot_plan: Identify 10 candidate accounts via AE referrals; qualify 5 for capacity pilot
Run 3-week and 6-week cohorts to compare conversion rates
Provide onboarding runbook and dedicated SE time during trial
Collect telemetry: utilization, p99 latency, burst events, overage frequency, net promoter feedback
Weekly check-ins with pilot customers and adjust pricing or caps if frequent overages observed
metrics_to_track: Average gross margin per micro-commit band
Overage frequency and average burst multiplier
Support escalations tied to SLA uplift
Time-to-sign (legal / SQ turnaround) for pilot deals
